intro: Chapter 3 of 1 Nephi opens immediately after Nephi's private vision: Lehi tells his sons they must return to Jerusalem to obtain the brass plates from Laban, which contain the Jewish scriptures and the family genealogy. Nephi responds with his famous declaration of faith — that God never gives a commandment without preparing a way for it to be accomplished. The chapter then traces two failed attempts to recover the plates: Laman is expelled from Laban's house at sword-point; a second attempt offering gold and silver ends with Laban stealing their property and sending servants to kill them. After fleeing into the wilderness, Nephi rallies his despairing brothers with an oath. The chapter closes with Laman and Lemuel beating Nephi and Sam with a rod — only to be stopped by an angel who rebukes them and promises that God will yet deliver Laban into their hands.
reading_tip: Three grammar constructions carry most of the chapter's theological weight. The narrative frame `چنین گذشت که` (and it came to pass) opens nearly every episode — once you recognize it, parsing each scene becomes automatic. The subjunctive after `تا` (so that / in order to) and after `مگر اینکه` (unless) signals purpose and condition respectively; watch for the `بـ-` prefix on the verb and the absence of `می-`. The future tense `خواه- + past-stem infinitive` (`خواهم رفت`, `خواهد سپرد`) appears for the first time in this chapter. Compound verbs are unusually dense here — `قرعه کشیدن`, `سر باز زدن`, `گرد هم آوردن`, `بدست آوردن` — so pay attention to the noun that precedes `کردن` or `شدن` as the key to the verb's meaning.

forms.desc: Persian uses the Indo-Persian digits `۰ ۱ ۲ ۳ ۴ ۵ ۶ ۷ ۸ ۹` (not the Arabic–Western `0–9`). Each digit's pronunciation is introduced at first appearance in this chapter.

entries.title: Grammar: Subjunctive after تا
entries.body: `تا` followed by a subjunctive verb means **"so that" or "in order to."** The verb loses its `می-` prefix and gains `بـ-` in the 3rd person forms. This construction signals purpose.

examples.persian: بازمی گردند تا ورقه‌های برنجی را بدست آورند
examples.translit: bāzmī-gardand tā varaqe-hā-ye berenǰī rā be-dast āvarand
examples.en: they return in order to obtain the brass plates

examples.persian: که بتوانند آنچه را که او به آنها فرمان می دهد به انجام برسانند

entries.title: Grammar: Passive voice with شدن
entries.body: Persian forms the passive with the **past participle** of the main verb + a conjugated form of `شدن` ("to become"). The passive agent, if stated, is introduced by `از سوی` ("by/from").

examples.persian: از سوی{e} یک فرشته سرزنش می شوند
examples.translit: az su-ye yek ferešte sarzaneš mī-šavand
examples.en: they are rebuked by an angel [past participle `سرزنش` + `می شوند`]

entries.title: Grammar: چنین گذشت که (and it came to pass)
entries.body: The phrase `چنین گذشت که` _čonīn gozašt ke_ — literally "thus it passed that" — is the Persian rendering of the Book of Mormon formula **"and it came to pass."** It introduces nearly every episode in the narrative. `چنین` means "thus/so"; `گذشت` is the past 3sg of `گذشتن` ("to pass"); `که` is the complementizer.

examples.persian: و چنین گذشت که من، نیفای، پس از سخن گفتن با سَروَر، به چادر پدرم بازگشتم
examples.translit: o čonīn gozašt ke man, Nīfāy, pas az soxan goftan bā Sarvar, be čādar-e pedar-am bāzgaštam
examples.en: And it came to pass that I, Nephi, having spoken with the Lord, returned to my father's tent

entries.meaning: to pass, go by; (time) to elapse

forms.desc: 3sg past `گذشت` _gozašt_ — appears in every `چنین گذشت که` formula

forms.note: As a complementizer (COMP), `که` introduces an embedded clause: `چنین گذشت که…` "it came to pass that…". As a relative particle (REL), it introduces relative clauses: `آنچه که…` "that which…".

entries.title: Grammar: Archaic narrative suffix `-ā` (گفتا)
entries.body: The Book of Mormon Persian uses the archaic literary suffix `-ā` on third-person past verbs to signal **narrative speech introduction**: `گفتا` _goftā_ = "he/she said" (emphatic narrative). This suffix is a relic of classical Persian poetry and formal prose and is not used in modern speech.

examples.persian: بر آنها سخن گفت، گفتا: چرا
examples.translit: bar ānhā soxan goft, goftā: čerā
examples.en: he spoke to them, saying: Why

`بر من سخن گفتن` = "to speak to me" (literally "to speak upon me") — a fixed expression with `سخن گفتن`.

entries.title: Grammar: Future tense (`خواه-` + past-stem infinitive)
entries.body:
The Persian future tense uses the present stem of `خواستن` ("to want") + the **past-stem infinitive** (past stem, no `-ن`). The auxiliary `خواه-` is conjugated for person/number; the infinitive is invariable and does not take `بـ-`.

| Person | Future | Gloss |
|---|---|---|
| 1sg | خواهم رفت | I will go |
| 2sg | خواهی بود | you will be |
| 3sg | خواهد سپرد | he/she will entrust |
| 1pl | نخواهیم رفت | we will not go |

The negative is formed by adding `ن-` to the auxiliary: `نخواهم رفت` _na-xāham raft_.

examples.translit: to mowred-e loṭf-e Sarvar xāhī bud

`به هستی … سوگند` "by the life of … (I swear)" — the prepositional phrase precedes the noun `سوگند` without a light verb in this usage

forms.note: `تا اینکه` + perfect subjunctive expresses a prerequisite: `نخواهیم رفت تا اینکه … رسانده باشیم` = "we will not go until we have accomplished…"

entries.meaning: to leave, leave behind; to place, put; (بگذارید) let (us), allow

etym.prose: `نگه` _negah_ (guard, look) + `داری` ← `داشتن` (to have/hold) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) suffix. Literally "the holding-guard."
from Arabic _īmān_ "faith, belief," root ā-m-n "to be secure, believe."
from Arabic _mīrāṯ_ "inheritance," root w-r-ṯ "to inherit."

forms.desc: `همه گونه` _hame-gune_ "all kinds of, every sort of" ([verse 16](#verse-16))

etym.prose: from Arabic _ṯarwa_ "wealth," root ṯ-r-w "to be wealthy."
from Arabic _bāqī_ "remaining," root b-q-y "to remain."
`سبب` _sabab_ from Arabic, root s-b-b "cause, reason."

entries.meaning: reason, cause; به سبب — because of

etym.prose: from Arabic _sabab_ "rope, reason, cause," root s-b-b.
`نا-` _nā-_ (negative prefix) + `بکار` _bekār_ (useful, doing good work) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) suffix. Literally "the quality of being of no use/good."

entries.meaning: to be destroyed, perish, be annihilated

etym.prose: `نا-` _nā-_ (negative prefix) + `بود` _bud_ (existence, being). Literally "to become not-existing."
`پیام` _payām_ (message) + `بر` _bar_ (carrier ← `بردن` "to carry"). Literally "message-carrier."
from Arabic _radd_ "rejection, return," root r-d-d "to reject."
from Arabic _halāk_ "destruction, ruin," root h-l-k "to perish."
`نا-` (negative) + `گزیر` _gozīr_ (option, escape ← `گزیدن` "to choose, bite"). Literally "without alternative."

entries.meaning: to stay, remain; to be left over

etym.prose: `خرد` _xerad_ (wisdom, intellect) + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) (possessing) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) suffix.
from Arabic _ḥifẓ_ "preservation, memorization," root ḥ-f-ẓ "to preserve, guard."

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 20 (`بیست` — a unique word, not "two-zero")

forms.note: 20 is a unique Persian word `بیست` _bīst_, not a compound of "two" + "zero."

etym.prose: from Arabic _muqaddas_ "sanctified," root q-d-s "to be holy."

entries.meaning: spirit, soul; روح مقدّس — Holy Ghost/Spirit

etym.prose: from Arabic _rūḥ_ "spirit, breath," root r-w-ḥ "to breathe, blow."
from Arabic _qudra_ "power, ability," root q-d-r "to be able, to have power."
from Arabic _zamān_ "time, era."
from Old Iranian; `آغاز` _āġāz_ (beginning, start) + `شدن` (to become).

entries.meaning: even; even up to, as far as
entries.warning: The final `ی` in `حتّی` is an _alif maqṣūra_ (Arabic ى spelled ی in Persian) — pronounced -ā, not -ī. Learners may accidentally read it as *_ḥattī_.

etym.prose: directly from Arabic _ḥattā_ "even, until, as far as."
`کنون` _konūn_ (now, at this moment) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-adjectival-suffix-i) adjectival suffix.

forms.desc: `با این شیوۀ زبان` = "with this manner of speaking" ([verse 21](#verse-21))

etym.prose: from Arabic _tarġīb_ "enticement, encouragement," root r-ġ-b "to desire, aspire."
`گران` _gerān_ (heavy, expensive) + `بها` _bahā_ (value, price). Literally "of heavy value."
`گرد` _gerd_ (round, together; gathered) + `آوردن` _āvardan_ (to bring). In the text the full phrase is `گرد هم آوردن` (with `هم` = together).

forms.desc: `هم` _ham_ in `گرد هم آوردن` intensifies the collective meaning: "to bring all together"

forms.note: `هم` as an intensifier in compound verbs: `گرد هم آوردن` (to gather together). As a standalone adverb: `من هم` "I too", `هم … هم` "both … and".

etym.prose: `دو` _do_ (two) + `باره` _bāre_ (time, occasion). Literally "a second time."

entries.meaning: place, room, spot; (به جای) instead of, in place of

forms.desc: `به جای آن` _be jā-ye ān_ "instead of it, in exchange for it" ([verse 24](#verse-24))

entries.meaning: much, many, a lot; too much, excessively

etym.prose: from Arabic _ziyād_ "increase, excess," root z-y-d "to increase."
from Arabic _hawas_ "obsession, craving," root h-w-s.
`خدمت` _xedmat_ (service, from Arabic _xidma_) + [`-گزار`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-gozar) (performer-of suffix ← `گذاشتن`).

entries.meaning: opposite, facing; equal; (از برابر) from in front of, away from

forms.desc: `از برابر` _az barābar-e_ "from in front of, fleeing from before" ([verse 26](#verse-26))
idiom: `پشت سر باقی بگذاریم` = "to leave behind" ([verse 26](#verse-26))

entries.meaning: to reach, arrive at; to attain

etym.prose: from Arabic _ṣaxra_ "rock, stone."
`گود` _gud_ (hollow, concave) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) noun suffix.

entries.meaning: also, likewise, in the same way
to accept, receive; to heed, take to heart

forms.desc: idiom: `بگوش دل می پذیرفت` _be-guš-e del mī-pazīroft_ "he heeded with his heart" (literally "was accepting to the ear of his heart") ([verse 28](#verse-28))

entries.meaning: very, much, many, a great deal
heart (seat of emotion and will); mind, spirit

forms.desc: `بگوش دل` _be-guš-e del_ "to the ear of the heart" — i.e. heeding wholeheartedly ([verse 28](#verse-28))

entries.title: Grammar: Relative clauses with که
entries.body: Persian relative clauses use `که` _ke_ immediately after the head noun. The head noun may carry an indefinite `-ī` suffix when it is the antecedent of a restrictive clause. The relative verb agrees with the head noun's implied referent.

examples.persian: سَروَر او را برگزیده است تا بر شما یک فرمانروا باشد
examples.translit: Sarvar u rā bar-gozīde ast tā bar šomā yek farmānravā bāšad
examples.en: the Lord has chosen him to be a ruler over you [تا introduces the purpose clause]

examples.persian: آنچه را که او به آنها فرمان می دهد
examples.translit: ānče rā ke u be ānhā farmān mī-dahad
examples.en: that which he commands them [آنچه = headless relative]

forms.note: Highly suppletive: infinitive `آمد-` but present stem is just `آ-` (_ā-_), as in `می آید` _mī-āyad_ "he/she comes."

entries.meaning: to stand, stop, come to a halt

forms.note: `آیا` at the start of a sentence marks it as a direct question: `آیا شما نمی دانید؟` = "Do you not know?" It has no meaning equivalent in English other than the rising intonation of a question.

etym.prose: preverb `بر-` + `گزیدن` _gozīdan_ (to select, choose).
`فرمان` _farmān_ (command) + `روا` _ravā_ (fitting, going — from `رفتن`). Literally "one for whom command is fitting"/"one who commands."

forms.note: `شما` is also used as a polite singular "you" (formal register).

forms.desc: `به دست` _be dast-e_ "into the hand/power of": `سَروَر لابان را به دست شما خواهد سپرد` ([verse 29](#verse-29))

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 30 (`سی` — a unique word, not "three-zero")

forms.note: `سی` _sī_ is the independent Persian word for 30.

entries.meaning: to set out, depart, take to the road

etym.prose: from Arabic _imkān_ "possibility" + `پذیر` _pazīr_ (accepting ← `پذیرفتن`).
`توانا` _tavānā_ (powerful, capable ← `توانستن`) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) suffix.

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 50 (`پنجاه` — unique word, not a compound)

etym.prose: `پنج` _panj_ (five) + `-اه/-اد` hundred-root suffix. The same pattern: `شصت` (60), `هفتاد` (70), `هشتاد` (80), `نود` (90).
`دستور` _dastur_ (order, instruction; minister — from Middle Persian _dastwar_ "authorized") + `دادن` _dādan_ (to give).

forms.note: `آری` is the formal/literary yes, used in classical and biblical register. Modern colloquial uses `بله` _bale_ or `آره` _āre_.

entries.meaning: then, at that time, in that case

forms.note: `آنگاه` is a formal/literary temporal adverb. Colloquial: `اون وقت` _un vaqt_.

entries.meaning: no; not (in short answers and rhetorical questions)

forms.note: `نه` at the end of a sentence in a rhetorical context = "isn't it?" or "then why not us?": `آنگاه چرا ما را نه؟` = "then why not us?" ([verse 31](#verse-31))

entries.meaning: to do, make; (light verb) performs the action named by the preceding noun

forms.note: The most common light verb in Persian. Dozens of Arabic nouns combine with `کردن` to form compound verbs: `قبول کردن` (to accept), `نصیحت کردن` (to advise), `تلاش کردن` (to try), etc.
